speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You are presenting with fatigue, abdominal pain, night sweats, weight loss, and enlarged supraclavicular lymph nodes; these are concerning for a serious underlying condition. To begin our evaluation, can you tell me your age and sex?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: The symptoms you describe—fever, night sweats, weight loss, and lymphadenopathy—are often referred to as "B symptoms," which are highly concerning. Given the location of the enlarged nodes and your age, I am particularly worried about a malignancy. Have you noticed any changes in your skin, such as yellowing or bruising, or any bleeding tendencies?

speaker: Patient
text: I noticed swelling in my neck over the last few days. It does not hurt, but it feels enlarged and fixed. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Tuberculosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: You mentioned a doctor suspected Tuberculosis, but the "fixed" and rapidly enlarging supraclavicular node is a classic sign of malignancy, specifically lymphoma or metastatic cancer. To differentiate between infection and cancer, I need to see the node and check your blood levels. REQUEST IMAGES: Neck ultrasound; REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential, LDH, and ESR.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Vital Signs: Temperature 36.8°C (98°F), Blood Pressure 135/80 mmHg, Heart Rate 82 bpm, Respiratory Rate 14 breaths/min. Physical Exam: Nontender, enlarged, and fixed supraclavicular lymph node; slight abdominal distension; splenomegaly detected without rebound tenderness; dullness over left lower quadrant. Lab Results: WBC Elevated, Hemoglobin Slightly Decreased, Platelets Normal, LDH Elevated. Imaging: CT Scan shows massively enlarged axillary, mediastinal, and cervical lymph nodes. Biopsy (Cervical Lymph Node): Lymphocytes with a high proliferative index positive for CD20.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The biopsy results showing CD20 positivity confirm a B-cell lymphoproliferative disorder, and the massive lymphadenopathy with splenomegaly is highly suggestive of Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma (DLBCL). Can you tell me if you have a history of any autoimmune diseases or recent infections that might have preceded these symptoms?

DIAGNOSIS READY: Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma (DLBCL)
